Sales Performance Dashboard: Stellar Enterprise

Practice project on a sample dataset. Power BI, Power Query, DAX. 3 report pages: Overview, Monthly Sales, Expenses.

$1.01bntotal sales
21.36%profit margin
6branches

The finished dashboard

Watch it in action

Problem and approach

The problem

A raw order file had to become something a manager can read in a minute: how much was sold, how much profit it made, where, and how each month compared with the one before.

From raw data to dashboard

1. The raw data

An Excel file with 1,212 orders and 15 columns (branch, category, product, sales channel, payment method, order status, quantity, price, discount, cost, total sales), January to December 2025.

It needed work: 12 duplicate orders, names typed in different ways (ABUJA, abuja, smart phones), 7 blank customer names, 6 blank discounts, and 25 totals that did not match quantity x price x (1 - discount).

2. What I built
  • Loaded the file into Power BI and standardised text with Power Query (for example Whatsapp, Ussd, Usb-C Hub).
  • Removed the 12 duplicate orders.
  • Added Total Cost, Net Sales, Gross Profit and Profit Margin columns.
  • Linked orders to a date table (month, month number, month start, month year) so months sort and compare correctly.
  • Wrote DAX measures for sales, profit, margin, average order, quantity, expenses and month-over-month change, comparing each month with the one before it.
  • Designed 3 dark-theme pages with KPI cards, trend lines, branch and category charts, an order-status donut, slicers and page buttons.
3. What it delivers

One report that answers 4 of the 10 business questions in the workbook: total, net sales and profit; which branch earns the most; the monthly trend; and how much is cancelled or returned. Category margins add a fifth angle.

Next version: sales channel, sales rep and discount views, since the data supports them.

Under the hood: data and model

Under the hood

Findings and recommendations

Findings

  • Total sales reached $1.01bn with a 21.36% profit margin. Net sales were $958.9M and profit was $215.9M.
  • Laptops brought in $466M, about 46% of sales, but had the lowest margin at 20.28%. Smartphones had the highest margin at 22.69%.
  • Lagos ($234M) and Abuja ($205M) led net sales. Enugu was lowest at $118M.
  • Sales peaked in August 2025 ($126M) and dipped in June ($62M). Month-over-month swings were large: May was up 39.7% on April, then June fell 41.6%.
  • In December, total sales fell 17.2% on November, net sales fell 16.8% and profit fell 20.5%. Profit margin dipped 3.9%.
  • Expenses totalled $742.9M. Laptops made up $346M of it and Lagos had the highest branch costs ($182M).
  • Costs moved with sales, peaking in August (about $94M). December costs were 15.7% lower than November.
  • About 34% of net sales were cancelled or returned ($164M and $160M), which points to an order fulfilment issue worth investigating.

What I would recommend

  • Find out why 34% of net sales are cancelled or returned, and fix the biggest cause first.
  • Review laptop pricing and costs. It is the biggest category but has the thinnest margin.
  • Plan stock and staffing for the August peak and the June dip.

Employee Training View

Practice project on a sample dataset. Power BI, Power Query, DAX. 2 report pages: Overview and Courses.

402training hours
100training sessions
12employees

The finished dashboard

Watch it in action

Problem and approach

The problem

Training records for employees were hard to review. HR needed to see how many people were trained, how many hours were spent, how well they scored, and which courses and training modes were used.

From raw data to dashboard

1. The raw data

An Excel file with 100 training records and 14 columns (employee, department, branch, manager, course, category, date, status, score, hours, mode). 12 employees and 5 courses, January to early June 2026.

It needed work: 39 records have no score because the training is not finished, and some entries were typed differently (" chinedu okoro", "completed", " online ", "it").

2. What I built
  • Loaded the file into Power BI as a Raw Data table.
  • Built a star-schema model: Raw Data linked one-to-many to Course data, Employee Data and Date tables (see Model view below).
  • Created measures: Total Employee, Total Training, Total Training hours, Total Courses and Average Assessment score.
  • Designed 2 pages with KPI cards, a monthly trend, donut, pie and bar charts, 4 slicers (month, course, training mode, status) and a page switcher.
3. What it delivers

HR can see in seconds how many sessions and hours were delivered, online versus classroom, who trained the most, and how each course category performs. Filtering updates every chart at once (see the demo video).

Next version: keep unscored trainings blank instead of 0, standardise names, and add department and branch views.

Under the hood: data and model

Under the hood

Findings and recommendations

Findings

  • 12 employees took 100 training sessions totalling 402 hours.
  • 61 of the 100 trainings are completed, 18 are in progress and 21 have not started.
  • Online training made up 54% of sessions and classroom 46%.
  • Technical courses had the most sessions (40 of 100).
  • Among the 61 scored trainings the average score is 73.8. Excel Fundamentals scored highest (82.0) and Power BI Essentials lowest (67.4).
  • Sessions peaked in January (28) and April (26). June shows only 7 because the data ends on 4 June.

Data note: the score cards in the screenshots show 45.03 because the 39 trainings without a score count as 0. The scores above come from the 61 scored trainings in the raw data.

What I would recommend

  • Follow up on the 21 trainings that have not started and the 18 still in progress.
  • Review Power BI Essentials, which has the lowest average score (67.4).
  • Plan sessions across the year. May had half the sessions of April.
